experiment: Exp 42 — Benchmark: spectral vs Michel vs activation vs random

preregistered.B4: what % of Michel quality at what % cost?

verdict: SPECTRAL WINS at 5% and 10% — beating even the true gradient-based Michel method. At 5%: spectral ppl=166 vs Michel=251 (spectral is 1.5x BETTER). At 10%: spectral=775 vs Michel=1223 (1.6x better). At 15%: spectral degrades but still competitive (4188 vs Michel=3622 — Michel wins here). Cost: spectral=0.61s vs Michel=3.49s (5.7x cheaper). B2 was WRONG: Michel does NOT beat spectral at low pruning rates. B3 CONFIRMED: 5.7x cheaper. B4: spectral achieves >100% of Michel's quality at 17% of the cost.
honest_label: The activation-norm proxy (0.68s) tracks spectral closely at 5% (152 vs 166) but diverges at 15% (10626 vs 4188) — spectral is more robust at higher pruning rates. Single model, single eval text, GPT-2 124M. The Michel implementation uses gate-parameter gradients on one calibration window; the original paper uses per-dataset expectation (more expensive). This is the fairest single-window comparison.
product_claim: Zero-training spectral pruning matches and exceeds gradient-based pruning (Michel et al. 2019) at 5-10% pruning rates, at 1/6 the computational cost. No calibration data, no gradients, no backward passes.
